channel.title: PaceOn Blog
channel.description: Straight talk on running training: pace, long runs, intervals and race preparation.

item.title: How to increase running mileage without getting injured
item.description: The 10% rule, down weeks and the warning signs that separate progression from injury. A guide to raising mileage safely.

item.title: Heart rate zones for running: a practical guide
item.description: What the five HR zones are, how to find yours without generic formulas, and how to use them to run truly easy and hard at the right time.

item.title: How many times a week should you run?
item.description: Three, four or five? It depends on your goal, your history and your recovery time. A straight guide to choosing the right frequency.

item.title: Recovery runs: what they are and when to do them
item.description: A short, very easy run the day after a hard workout speeds up recovery — if it's truly done slowly. How, how much and when.

item.title: How to calculate running pace (with examples)
item.description: Pace is time per kilometer. Learn to calculate it, convert to speed, predict race times and use our free calculator.

item.title: What the long run is and why it matters
item.description: The longest run of the week builds endurance no other workout builds. How far to run, at what pace and how to progress without getting hurt.

item.title: What interval training is and how to do it
item.description: Hard stretches alternated with recovery: how intervals work, examples by goal and the mistakes that cancel out the workout.

item.title: How to prepare for a half marathon
item.description: Base, build, peak and taper: how to organize 12 to 16 weeks to reach 21 km with the right long run, no injury and a strategy.

item.title: How to train for a 10K: plan and strategy
item.description: A 10-to-12-week structure to finish or improve your 10K time: volume, key workouts, taper and race strategy.

item.title: How to improve your running pace
item.description: Why running faster every day doesn't make you faster, and which stimuli actually lower your pace consistently.

item.title: How to run a 5K from scratch in 8 weeks
item.description: A realistic 8-week plan to go from sedentary to finishing your first 5 km running, with safe progression and no overreach.
